sections.heading: Two's complement in one line
points: Negate by flipping every bit and adding one.
The top bit has weight -2^(n-1); the rest are positive as usual.
n bits cover -2^(n-1) .. +2^(n-1)-1, so 8 bits give -128 .. +127.

sections.heading: Why it won
points: One zero, not two (sign-and-magnitude has +0 and -0).
a - b is just a + (-b), so one adder does both operations.
Negation is a row of inverters plus a carry-in of 1.

sections.heading: Patterns worth recognising
points: 10000000 = -128 in 8 bits: the most negative value, with no positive twin.
Sign extension copies the sign bit into the new high bits.

sections.heading: Traps the quiz likes
points: Overflow and carry are different flags.
Two positives giving a negative is signed overflow.
Widening a negative byte with zeros turns it into a big positive number.
